verses.1: These are the words of Lemuel, king of Massa, which his mother taught him.
verses.2: What, my son, is your strength, and what, son of my womb, is the strength of your youth?
verses.3: Do not give your strength to women, nor your ways to those who destroy kings.
verses.4: Do not let kings, O Lemuel, drink wine, nor let rulers desire alcohol.
verses.5: Lest they drink and forget what is written, and twist the judgment of all the afflicted.
verses.6: Give alcohol to the one who is perishing, and wine to one whose soul is bitter.
verses.7: Let him drink and forget his poverty, and his sorrow no longer be remembered.
verses.8: Open your mouth for the silent, for the judgment of all the poor.
verses.9: Open your mouth, speak just judgment, and declare the right for the afflicted and the poor.
verses.10: Who can find a woman of valor? Her price is far beyond that of pearls.
verses.11: Her husband trusts in her, and he lacks no treasure.
verses.12: She does good and not evil, all the days of her life.
verses.13: She seeks wool and flax, and works with her hands in delight.
verses.14: She is like merchant ships, bringing her bread from afar.
verses.15: She rises while it is still night, giving food to her household and portions to her servant girls.
verses.16: She considers a field and buys it, with the fruit of her hands she plants a vineyard.
verses.17: She puts on strength like armor, and strengthens her arms.
verses.18: She tastes that her trade is good, her lamp does not go out through the night.
verses.19: Her hands reach for the distaff, and her hands support the spindle.
verses.20: She opens her hand to the poor, and extends her hands to the afflicted.
verses.21: She is not afraid for her household because of snow, for all her household is clothed in double.
verses.22: She makes herself coverings of embroidered cloth, her clothing is fine linen and silk.
verses.23: Her husband is known at the gates, sitting among the elders of the land.
verses.24: She makes herself coverings and sells them, and delivers sashes to the merchants.
verses.25: Strength and dignity are her clothing, and she laughs at the time to come.
verses.26: She opens her mouth with wisdom, and the teaching of kindness is on her tongue.
verses.27: She watches over the ways of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness.
verses.28: Her sons honor her, her husband praises her.
verses.29: Many women have done valiantly, but you surpass them all.
verses.30: Deceit is the beauty, and vanity is the appearance. But a woman who fears the LORD, she shall be praised.
verses.31: Give her of the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her in the gates.

notes:
Notes
- v. 2: "son of my womb" is a poetic expression for deep personal connection, rendered as such.
- v. 30: "fears the LORD" is a standard Hebrew idiom for reverent, obedient devotion.
- v. 30: "she shall be praised" preserves the Hebrew "tithallel," which is reflexive and emphasizes her being celebrated.
